title: SLO burn visualization + incident playback — UX grooming notes
content:
Context and goal:
- Problem: on-call and engineering teams want faster context when an SLO alert fires — not just the raw metric but the sequence of events and policy routing decisions that led to the noisy page.
- Goal: prototype a compact SLO burn + incident playback experience inside Console that helps triage, reroute, and tune policies from one surface. Reduce time-to-meaning for a page and make policy impact visible.

High-level concept:
- A single card per alerting incident that combines:
  1) SLO burnline sparkline (30/90/365d baseline toggles) + instant burn rate annotation,
  2) Collapsible incident timeline (events, policy-evaluations, notification sends),
  3) Routing map (which contact/rotation/channel received the message, and fallbacks taken),
  4) Quick actions: mute/ack/reassign/duplicate-as-followup, and an inline policy-tweak simulation.

Why this is different from existing pages:
- We avoid large separate policy editors — instead embed a minimal "what-if" simulator: change threshold/hold-time/fanout and run a dry simulation on the recorded incident to see who would have been notified and whether SLO breach would still have triggered.
- Incident playback is sequence-first rather than metric-first: let users scrub a timeline and watch the changes in burn and routing evolve.

Low-fidelity wireframe notes (textual):
- Card header: incident title, SLO name, severity tag, time since start, short summary (eg. "svc-x increased error rate, burn spike -> page").
- Left column (compact): vertical sparkline with colored regions (green/yellow/red), numeric % of SLO burned, & baseline selector (toggle: 30d/90d/custom).
- Middle column (expandable): timeline lane w/ stacked rows: metric markers, evaluation checkpoints (rule evaluated true/false), notification events, external signals (deploys, infra changes). Each event has a hover tooltip with details and a small icon for type.
- Right column (actions + routing): list of recipients hit in order with channel icons, and a small badge showing if fallback or escalation was used. Buttons: "Mute for 1h", "Acknowledge", "Open follow-up" and a tiny "Simulate policy change" link.
- Timeline scrubber: play/pause with speed control. Scrubbing updates the sparkline focus and highlights which notifications were live at that time.

Key UX interactions to validate in prototype:
- Scrubbing should be low-latency (<100ms feel) and update recipient highlights. Trying to emulate video-like playback but with event stepping.
- Simulate-policy modal: quick inputs only (threshold %, hold seconds, route order). On "Run simulation" show a diff: who would have been notified vs who were actually notified and whether the page would have been suppressed.
- Inline link to the policy used (deep link to full policy composer).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- [ ] Card shows SLO burnline and sparkline with baseline toggles.
- [ ] Incident timeline shows metric points, policy-evaluations, and notification events for last 72h.
- [ ] Playback scrubber works and highlights recipients as timeline moves.
- [ ] Simulate-policy returns a simple diff and UX shows expected impact on notification count and whether page suppresses.
- [ ] UX hooks to mute/ack/reassign from card.

Backlog grooming (candidate tickets + rough sizing):
- INF-3101: "SLO burn sparkline component" — 3 pts — data API + small viz (owner: Maya)
- INF-3102: "Incident timeline events feed (72h)" — 5 pts — ensure order, event typing, and hover metadata (owner: Ethan)
- INF-3103: "Playback scrubber + recipient highlight" — 5 pts — client-side stepping and keyframe interpolation (owner: Priya)
- INF-3104: "Policy simulation endpoint" — 8 pts — server sim engine (accepts recorded events + candidate policy change) (owner: eng-applied-ml)
- INF-3105: "Compact routing list + quick actions" — 2 pts — UI and wiring to existing notification APIs (owner: console-team)
- INF-3106: "Telemetry for playback interactions" — 2 pts — capture scrub, simulate, and mute actions for evaluation.

Open questions / risks:
- Data retention: timeline requires events and policy-eval traces — how long do we keep these? 90d? cost concerns.
- Privacy/tenant isolation: recorded events sometimes include recipient identifiers. Need redaction or role-based access for playback and simulation.
- Simulation fidelity: can we guarantee exact parity with production routing? If not, label results as "best-effort" and include a conf-level.
- Performance: streaming playback over large event windows could be heavy — consider pre-computed sparse keyframes for >24h incidents.

Edge cases to think about:
- Multi-tenant alerts where policy inheritance influences routing — playback should visualize whether tenant policy overrode org default.
- Chain reactions: a single deploy triggers multiple degradations — allow filtering timeline by source type (deploys, infra, metric).
- Pager rotations with scheduled overrides (someone out of office) — simulation should respect calendar overrides if possible (or show as uncertain).

User testing plan (early prototype):
- Target participants: 6 on-call engineers + 4 platform owners.
- Tasks: triage an historical incident with current console vs prototype playback; run a simulation to reduce noise; create a follow-up runbook.
- Success metrics: time to first-action (reduce by 30%), perceived confidence in routing explanation (qual >4/5).

Next steps and owners:
- Wireframe clickable Figma by 2026-02-02 — owner: Maya.
- Backend design doc for simulation API by 2026-02-09 — owner: Ethan.
- Spike: client playback perf (can we get 50ms step updates for 1k events?) — owner: Priya — due 2026-02-16.
- Schedule 1-hour cross-team review: calendar invite INF-playback-review (attendees: product, SRE, eng-applied-ml, privacy).

Notes to self / rough thoughts:
- Might be useful to add a tiny "cost impact" estimate (how many notifications were sent * channel cost) to help teams balance policies.
- Consider an "automation suggestion" card: if simulation shows 90% of pages would be avoided by adding 2m hold, suggest a policy change with one-click apply + audit. Need strict guardrails.
- Keep the initial UI compact; avoid creating a separate large modal unless user explicitly wants to deep-dive.

References and similar patterns observed elsewhere:
- Playback feels like a condensed version of Zoom/Meeting replay (scrub + events), and similar to incident timeline features in other SRE tooling.
- Policy simulation is inspired by feature-flag "preview" flows — keep it ephemeral and clearly labeled.

PRIORITY: medium — shipping this would improve triage flow and reduce noisy pages but depends on simulation backend and event retention policy decisions.
